record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove in full generality that the ultraviolet limit of four-dimensional φ⁴ theory is trivial.

evidence.quote: Can one prove in full generality that its ultraviolet limit is trivial

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d=4$ and, for a finite hypercubic lattice $\Lambda \subset a\mathbb{Z}^4$ with spacing $a>0$, consider the lattice $\varphi^4$ measure on $\mathbb{R}^\Lambda$ given by
$$d\mu_{\Lambda,a,g,\mu_0}(\varphi) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z}\exp\!\Big(-a^4\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\big(\tfrac{1}{2}|\nabla_a\varphi(x)|^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\mu_0\,\varphi(x)^2 + g\,\varphi(x)^4\big)\Big)\prod_{x\in\Lambda} d\varphi(x),$$
where $\nabla_a$ is the discrete gradient, $g>0$, and $\mu_0\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\langle\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\Lambda,a,g,\mu_0}$ denote the corresponding expectation, and let $\mu(\Lambda\to\mathbb{R}^4,\,a\to 0,\,g,\mu_0)$ be any continuum probability measure on $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^4)$ obtained as a (subsequential) joint thermodynamic and ultraviolet limit of these lattice measures, with the bare parameters $g=g(a)>0$ and $\mu_0=\mu_0(a)$ tuned so that the limiting two-point Schwinger function is non-degenerate (i.e., the limit defines a non-trivial generalized random field with Euclidean invariance).

Prove, in full generality (for every choice of bare-parameter trajectory $(g(a),\mu_0(a))$ producing such a continuum limit), that any limit measure $\mu$ obtained in this way is Gaussian. Equivalently, show that all connected Schwinger functions of order $\ge 4$ of the limit vanish, so that the resulting Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^4$ is necessarily a (generalized) free field.
artifact.category_tag: Constructive quantum field theory / phi^4 triviality
artifact.status_search_result: Aizenman and Duminil-Copin (Annals of Math. 194 (2021), 163–235) proved marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and lattice $\varphi^4_4$ models with nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic interaction, essentially settling the symmetric single-component case approached from the symmetric (high-temperature/critical) side. A 2023 follow-up (arXiv:2309.05797) extends triviality results. However, the fully general statement covering all UV limits and parameter regimes (e.g., broken-symmetry phase, non-ferromagnetic or non-nearest-neighbor variants, vector $N$-component models) is not entirely settled, so the problem in full generality is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and φ^4_4 models
status_evidence.snippet: Aizenman and Duminil-Copin prove that scaling limits of nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising and lattice φ^4 models in 4D are Gaussian.
status_evidence.claim: Marginal triviality of φ^4_4 was proved for the standard nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic case.

status_evidence.title: Triviality of the scaling limits of critical Ising and φ^4 models
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work extending triviality results for critical Ising and φ^4 models.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to extend the scope of triviality results, indicating the general program is still being completed.

status_evidence.title: Corrigendum: Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and φ_4^4 models
status_evidence.snippet: A 2024 corrigendum to the 2021 Annals paper.
status_evidence.claim: The proof has been refined since 2021, indicating active completion of the program.
